articles.headline: Brentford vs. Chelsea LIVE: Premier League updates as Danny Welbeck, Jordan Henderson start for Chelsea
articles.description: Brentford host London rivals Chelsea in the Premier League's Friday evening action, and you can follow live with ESPN.
articles.body:
Brentford host London rivals Chelsea in the Premier League's Friday evening action, and you can follow live with ESPN.

The hosts are one place and one point behind Chelsea in the table in seventh, though both sides can go third, if only temporarily, with a win at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Chelsea are coming off a defeat to Arsenal and a draw with newly-promoted Hull City in the league, while Brentford are unbeaten so far this term.

- Xabi Alonso thanks Todd Boehly, Mark Walter after Chelsea sale

- João Pedro withdraws from Brazil squad with injury

It's been another eventful week behind the scenes at Chelsea with the news that co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter have sold their stakes in the club. 

Boehly and Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea -- having each owned 12.83% -- to give Clearlake Capital -- which previously held 61.5% -- full control of the London club.

The consortium bought Chelsea in 2022 for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion), with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment. The club's sale came after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned by alleged ties to Russia president Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, will remain a partner in the ownership group, the club has confirmed.

Chelsea manager Alonso said it was time to "move on together."

"I think it is an important day for the club when there is an important change in the structure of the club, new ownership," Alonso told a news conference on Thursday.

"Thanks to the former owners for what they have done. I was not here but I know that they played an important role. And now that Behdad [Eghbali] is taking more control, or almost full control, I think it is good that the main one is clear."

articles.headline: QB Burrow good to go, DE Stewart set for Bengals debut vs. Texans
articles.description: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back) was a full participant at Friday's practice and is set to start in Sunday's road affair against the Texans.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- The Bengals will officially have their starting quarterback this weekend.

Joe Burrow was a full participant at Friday's practice and is set to play in this week's road contest against the Houston Texans, coach Zac Taylor said. Burrow was limited on Wednesday and Thursday with back tightness that flared up following the team's Week 1 win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Taylor said he "feels good" about Burrow's availability for the game and doesn't feel as if Burrow needs to mitigate injury risk, whether it be this weekend or moving forward.

"He's a competitor," Taylor said. "Take that from him and now what do you have? You got a guy who you've taken the stinger out of him a little bit. I'm not about that."

In the first game of the season, Burrow was 25-of-35 for 254 yards, one touchdown and an interception that was returned for a touchdown. He was sacked once and took very few hits -- with the exception of one scramble.

Near the end of the first quarter, Burrow scrambled for six yards to convert a third down. He was hit hard by Tampa Bay linebacker Alex Anzalone at the intersection of the sideline and the first-down marker.

Taylor used that play as an example of Burrow's competitiveness.

"He's got to go play football," Taylor said. "This is the NFL. And of course we want him to be safe and healthy. I'm not comfortable saying don't go get the first down on third eight and be two yards short and (then) let's go for it."

Throughout the week, Burrow strongly indicated that he would be healthy enough to play against the Texans despite the limited usage early in the week. On Wednesday, he made no significant throws before ramping up as the week went on.

Burrow said dealing with an injury like the one he is dealing with is just part of the game.

"People that play tackle football from third grade, like I did, and all contact sports, it's part of part of the game," Burrow said on Wednesday. "So, we've been dealing with this since we were little. It's no big deal."

The Bengals are looking to start the season with a 2-0 record for the second straight year. This year could yield a more optimistic outlook, however. In last year's Week 2 victory, Burrow sustained a turf toe injury that sidelined him for the following nine weeks. That marked the third time in his career that he landed on injured reserve (2020, knee; 2023, wrist).

In other injury news, Bengals defensive end Shemar Stewart will make his season debut. He missed the first game as he continued to recover from a hyperextended left knee that he suffered on the first practice of training camp.

"Obviously the talent we drafted in the first round, that's why he's here," Taylor said. "And so I'm just excited to get him back in the fold and get him some reps."

Bengals defensive tackle B.J. Hill is expected to be listed as questionable after dealing with Achilles soreness on Thursday, Taylor said. He did not practice on Friday.

articles.headline: Sources: Jazz, Keyonte George agree to 5-year, $157.5M extension
articles.description: The Utah Jazz and guard Keyonte George have agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million contract extension, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
Guard Keyonte George has agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million contract extension with the Utah Jazz, sources told ESPN.

The deal does not include a team or player option, sources said. The terms were finalized Friday after months of negotiations between George's agent Jason Ranne of The Team and Jazz president of basketball operations Austin Ainge.

George's new deal will account for approximately 16 percent of Utah's salary cap.

George, 22, the 16th overall pick in the 2023 draft, cemented himself as an essential piece of the franchise's foundation with a breakout campaign last season. He averaged 23.6 points and 6.1 assists per game while shooting 45.6% from the floor and 37.1% from 3-point range -- all career bests.

The Jazz envision George and Darryn Peterson, the No. 2 pick in this year's draft, emerging as one of the league's most dynamic backcourt duos.

Utah, which endured a rebuilding process in recent years, hopes to make a major leap toward competitiveness this season after acquiring two-time All-Star power forward Jaren Jackson Jr. at the trade deadline.

articles.headline: Lamine Yamal reveals he has experienced racism 'a thousand times'
articles.description: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has revealed that he has experienced racism "a thousand times."
articles.body:
Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has revealed that he has experienced racism "a thousand times."

The 19-year-old said people can sometimes be "indirectly racist" and "without realising it," whilst stressing that "what is wrong can never be accepted."

The World Cup winner, who has started this season in fine form for Barcelona, scoring seven goals in six La Liga matches, spoke in an interview with Movistar, which will be broadcast on Sept. 18 in Spain about the subject of racism.

In extracts shown on social media, Yamal said: "A thousand times [I've experienced racism].

"People are indirectly racist towards you, even though they don't realise it. There are lots of comments or looks that are racist, and they don't realise it."

Yamal has quickly become one of the most iconic faces in football after rising to prominence during the 2024 Euros, which Spain also won.

And he explains now that while he does not accept racism, he is no longer phased by it.

"I'm at a place where, it's not that it's accepted, because you can never accept something that's wrong, but it doesn't bother you [when it happens]," he added.

Yamal spoke further on a specific example of being unfazed by the comments, describing a time when he did not react despite being called Black by an opposition fan.

- Harry Kane on Ballon d'Or: 73 goals last season 'speaks for itself'

- Man City's Enzo Maresca: 'If I don't win it's a disaster'

- Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta on Fabian Hürzeler falling out: 'That's all in the past'

People ended up surprised by Yamal's lack of reaction but he explained why he did not react.

"There's that well-known video from the Bernabéu where people were shouting all sorts of things at Raphinha and me, and everyone was surprised by my reaction," he said.

"Being called 'Black' doesn't bother me in the slightest -- I am Black, after all.

"It's another matter entirely that it's wrong, because he's saying it to offend me, but if I'm playing a match and he's paid for a ticket to watch me, I'm not going to get angry just because I've been disrespected."

articles.headline: With Penix not ready, Rush getting second start for Falcons
articles.description: The Falcons will start quarterback Cooper Rush for the second straight week, coach Kevin Stefanski said Friday.
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- The Atlanta Falcons will start quarterback Cooper Rush for the second straight week, coach Kevin Stefanski said Friday.

Rush will get the start against the NFC South rival Carolina Panthers on Sunday with Michael Penix Jr. (ACL) not quite ready just yet. The Falcons left open the possibility of Penix returning earlier this week. Rush started in Week 1, a 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Tua Tagovailoa (oblique), who won the starting job out of training camp, did not practice this week and will be ruled out. He suffered the injury in practice last week and has not been back yet.

During the media viewing portion of practice Friday, Rush was throwing in the routes-on-air drill to the first-team receivers, with backup Jack Strand getting a few passes in, as well. Penix was throwing to the scout team receivers.

Rush has also been dealing with back spasms, which flared up last Saturday. Stefanski said he "wouldn't speculate" on Rush's health, but he has practiced fully and "doing better."

On Penix, Stefanski said, "It's a progression. Feel really confident in the plan."

Rush was 12-of-22 for 143 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions last week. His ESPN QBR was 2.6, the worst mark in the league in Week 1.

Undrafted rookie Strand will be the backup quarterback Sunday, Stefanski said.

articles.headline: Ex-U.S. youth defender Noahkai Banks picks Germany over USMNT
articles.description: The German Football Federation announced on Friday that coveted dual national defender Noahkai Banks has pledged his international future to Germany over the United States.
articles.body:
The German Football Federation announced on Friday that coveted dual-national defender Noahkai Banks has pledged his international future to Germany over the United States.

In a news release, Germany under-21 coach Antonio Di Salvo said that both Banks and Tunisian dual-national forward Louey Ben Farhat of Karlsruher SC have "chosen to represent Germany."

- Sullivan, USMNT's gifted next generation kick-start road to 2030 World Cup

- Red Bulls teen Hall undecided on USMNT future despite 1st call-up

- Teen Sullivan in USMNT squad, Pulisic left out

"We've been in contact with both of them for a while now and had focused our efforts on them," Di Salvo said in a statement. "I'm very pleased that we have been able to lay out a future pathway with Germany for them and that they agreed with it."

The news of Banks' decision will come as a disappointment to the U.S. men's national team program, which remains thin at center back.

Banks previously represented the U.S. at the 2023 U17 World Cup, meaning he'll have to file a one-time change of association with FIFA in order to make his choice official. According to a FIFA portal tracking changes of association, as of Friday Banks' request hadn't yet gone through.

Banks, 19, was born in Honolulu, Hawaii, to an American father and German mother, but in an interview with ESPN in February, Banks' mother Nadine Kinkel said the family moved back to Germany when Noahkai was seven-weeks old. While Banks traveled regularly to the U.S. to visit his father Sedrick, he has lived in Germany most of his life, and rose through the ranks of FC Augsburg starting at age nine. Banks has so far made 35 appearances in all competitions for Augsburg, scoring one goal.

Following Banks' participation in the 2023 U17 World Cup, the USMNT maintained contact with Banks, and he appeared for the U.S. U19 and U20 teams. Those efforts intensified after his breakthrough with Bundesliga side Augsburg last season. Banks was called in by U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino for a training camp in September 2025, but didn't appear in matches against South Korea and Japan.

At the time, the outreach appeared to be paying off.

"I really enjoyed the camp, to be honest, because I thought as a young guy, maybe I will get treated differently," Banks told ESPN in February. "But how the guys helped me to get into the team and into the training, it was incredible, to be honest. Also, the big guys like Christian Pulisic or Tim Weah, we maybe don't expect it, but it has been great."

But Germany soon upped its recruiting efforts. Banks was thought to have a strong chance of making the U.S. roster for the 2026 World Cup, but he turned down an invite to U.S. camp in March. Banks later said he wasn't ready to make a decision on his international future, and thus ruled himself out of possibly playing for the U.S. at the World Cup.

articles.headline: Stephon Gilmore, '19 NFL DPOY, retiring as member of the Patriots
articles.description: Stephon Gilmore, a two-time All-Pro cornerback and the NFL's 2019 Defensive Player of the Year, is signing a one-day contract in New England to retire as a member of the Patriots,
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Stephon Gilmore wasn't known for being much of a talker during his 13 NFL seasons.

But one of the most dominant cornerbacks of his era is officially retiring with the team with whom he had the most success during his career.

The 35-year-old Gilmore is returning to New England on Friday to sign a one-day contract and retire as a member of the Patriots, the team he won his lone Super Bowl with to cap the 2018 season.

Gilmore last played in 2024 with the Minnesota Vikings and previously announced his retirement in April via an Instagram post.

Selected 10th in the 2012 draft by the Buffalo Bills, Gilmore established himself as one of the league's premier players in the secondary over the next five seasons.

Gilmore was an instant standout in New England's secondary after arriving as a free agent from Buffalo in 2017.

He earned the first of two straight AP All-Pro selections in his second season with the Patriots in 2018. He also had the game-clinching interception late in the fourth quarter of New England's 13-3 Super Bowl win over the Los Angeles Rams to cap that season.

In 2019 he became the first player in Patriots history to be named NFL Defensive Player of the Year, leading the league with a career-high six interceptions, two returned for touchdowns. In addition, he had a career-high 20 pass breakups in both 2018 and 2019.

He was traded to the Carolina Panthers during the 2021 season.

His career includes stints with the Bills (2012-16), Patriots (2017-20), Panthers (2021), Indianapolis Colts (2022), Dallas Cowboys (2023) and Vikings (2024).

The five-time Pro Bowl selection ends his career with 32 interceptions and 149 pass breakups.

articles.headline: Commanders rule out Frankie Luvu, Chig Okonkwo vs. Cowboys
articles.description: The Commanders have ruled out linebacker Frankie Luvu, and tight end Chig Okonkwo for Sunday's road game against Dallas, coach Dan Quinn said.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The Washington Commanders have ruled out linebacker Frankie Luvu, and tight end Chig Okonkwo for Sunday's road game against Dallas, coach Dan Quinn said.

Luvu injured his groin and Okonkwo his hamstring in Sunday's loss at Philadelphia. Neither player practiced this week, though both worked some with the athletic trainers on a separate field Friday.

Okonkwo's absence impacts the pass game, as Washington signed him in the offseason to be a potential explosive target -- especially when the Commanders use play action. He caught two passes for 16 yards against the Eagles before leaving late in the third quarter.

Among replacements, John Bates is considered a strong blocker but has only 74 career receptions in 83 games, while Ben Sinnott and Colson Yankoff have a combined 18 receptions since entering the NFL in 2024.

The Commanders also could use heavy three-receiver sets; they used such looks on 71.6% of their plays vs. the Eagles.

Luvu served as the defensive play caller against the Eagles, recording a sack in his two quarters of action. He has started 35 games since signing with the Commanders in the 2024 offseason.

Washington's defense under new coordinator Daronte Jones relies heavily on its linebackers to be blitzers and edge rushers. The Commanders like their depth at the position -- even with another inside linebacker, Jordan Magee, having been placed on injured reserve earlier in the week because of a hamstring injury.

The Commanders will start Leo Chenal, signed as a free agent this offseason, and rookie Sonny Styles, the seventh overall pick in the draft who sacked the Eagles' Jalen Hurts last week. Second-year Kain Medrano will be the third linebacker.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA free agency: Grades for offseason signings, extensions
articles.description: We're grading the biggest free agent signings and extensions, including Keyonte George's extension with the Jazz.
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

 Sept. 18: George, Jazz agree to extension 

Keyonte George terms: Five years, $157.5 million

Grade: C+

George was one of the breakout players of the 2025-26 season, averaging 23.6 points and 6.1 assists per game while making 37% of his 3-pointers. He also boosted his efficiency from 7-8% below average in his first two seasons to 5% above average last year, which made him one of the top offensive guards in the sport.

On its own, that trajectory -- combined with George's age, as he'll turn 23 in November -- makes him more than worthy of this new rookie extension, which will pay him an average of $31.5 million per year. For context, this contract will pay nearly $100 million less over half a decade compared to the possible 25% max (which Victor Wembanyama, another member of the 2023 draft class, signed earlier this offseason).

But the complication with analyzing George's new deal is uncertainty about his ability on the other end. The Jazz have been worse with George on the floor versus when he's off in every season of his career to date. The defensive swing has been particularly problematic: Per Cleaning the Glass, Utah's defensive rating was 6.7 points worse with George last season and 8.7 points worse in 2024-25. Both marks ranked in the bottom 10% of players leaguewide.

Because of that track record, advanced stats that factor in on/off data are much lower in their assessment of George than his shiny box score stats would suggest. DARKO rates George as the third-least-valuable defender in the league, and both estimated plus-minus and xRAPM put him all the way in last place. Other players in his range include the likes of Cam Thomas and Trae Young, who have proved difficult to build around because of their limitations.

It's possible that this indictment of George is attributable to Utah's noncompetitive status during his time there; the Jazz haven't exactly been concerned about finishing 30th, 29th and 29th on defense over the last three years, as they've sought high draft picks instead of regular-season wins. articles.headline: Cavaliers promote Brandon Weems to general manager
articles.description: The Cavaliers are promoting Brandon Weems, who has been with the team for the past decade, to serve as general manager.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers have promoted Brandon Weems to serve as general manager under team president Koby Altman, the team announced Friday.

Weems has been in the Cavaliers organization for the past decade, rising from scouting and personnel positions to be the team's assistant general manager since 2022. He replaces Mike Gansey, who was hired as the Philadelphia 76ers' president of basketball operations in May.

"Brandon has earned this opportunity through more than a decade of exceptional work with the Cavaliers and by consistently demonstrating elite judgment and the expertise required to help lead our basketball operations," Altman said in a statement. "He has been instrumental in our player evaluation and roster-building processes, has a deep understanding of our culture, and has grown into a tremendous leader."

Weems, 40, is a childhood friend and former high school teammate of LeBron James. James' agent, Rich Paul, referred to Weems as "basically LeBron's brother" during the superstar's free agency process this summer. Paul indicated that Weems' presence was a pro in the Cavaliers' pursuit before James ultimately chose to sign with the 76ers.

James congratulated Weems on social media for getting the general manager job, writing "YESSIR!!!! Congratulations my brother @BrandonWeems10!! Proud of you man."

Among the other moves in the front office Friday, the Cavaliers named former NBA player Jose Calderon to assistant general manager. Calderon had served as a special adviser to the front office since 2022.

Prior to joining the Cavaliers, Weems was an assistant coach at Oakland University. He has also served on the staffs at Drexel and Kentucky, where he worked under coach John Calipari.

He played college basketball at Walsh University, winning an NAIA title in 2005.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA buzz: Latest free agency and trade updates
articles.description: We're tracking deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including the latest on Kawhi Leonard and the NBA's investigation into the Clippers.
articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 18

Jazz, George agree on a five-year, rookie-scale extension

Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George have agreed on a five-year, $157.5 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Tim MacMahon. George was the No. 16 pick in the 2023 draft and has averaged 17.2 points and 5.3 assists per game in his three seasons with the Jazz.

Sept. 17

Bey, Pelicans agree to three-year extension

New Orleans Pelicans' Saddiq Bey agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a trade kicker, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Bey averaged a career-high 17.7 points per game last season after missing all of the 2024-25 season with a torn ACL.

Sept. 16

Kings remain interested in Duren

The Sacramento Kings continue to loom in the background of Jalen Duren's restricted free agency with the incumbent Detroit Pistons.

Kings general manager Scott Perry met with Duren for dinner in Miami in early July and has maintained a level of steady interest in the ultimate outcome of Duren's free agency, though a path to acquire Duren this summer remains blocked.

The Pistons declined any legitimate conversation about a Duren sign-and-trade to the Kings for starting center Domantas Sabonis and have maintained a strong stance about their intention to keep Duren.

As ESPN reported earlier this month, the Pistons have a five-year offer in the $35 million per year range on the table, but that hasn't been enough to entice the disgruntled Duren to sign.

His greatest piece of leverage is a risky one -- the $9.6 million qualifying offer that would make him an unrestricted free agent next summer, when Sacramento will have flexibility for the first time in Perry's tenure as general manager. Zach LaVine's $48.9 million contract and De'Andre Hunter's $24.9 million contract both expire, allowing the Kings to generate a max offer for Duren, should he be available.

But that would only be the case if Duren is willing to take a massive one-year paycut and accept the risk of the qualifying offer. Until then, the Kings remain in the background as an interested long-term suitor helping Duren's leverage. -- Anthon

articles.headline: Dominic Calvert-Lewin is 'like a good wine,' says Leeds boss Daniel Farke
articles.description: Daniel Farke said Dominic Calvert-Lewin is "like a good wine" following the in-form striker's call-up into Thomas Tuchel's England squad.
articles.body:
Daniel Farke said Dominic Calvert-Lewin is "like a good wine" following the in-form striker's call-up into Thomas Tuchel's England squad.

The 29-year-old has been included in the Three Lions' squad for their upcoming Nations League matches after scoring four goals in six appearances in all competitions this season.

He was given a standing ovation by Leeds fans as he was withdrawn late on in Monday night's 4-1 win against Newcastle at Elland Road, while Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher described him as "unplayable."

Farke said: "Dominic is like a good wine, getting better by the year. Physically, he's on a top level and his pace is more than good enough I would say. He's a very complete striker."

Calvert-Lewin arrived at Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in August last year and when asked where he ranked among his best-ever signings, Farke said: "At Leeds while I've been here we've made many top signings on a low budget.

"When I think about Joe Rodon, Ethan Ampadu, Ao Tanaka. It's difficult to compare because as a striker you have a different role. But he's definitely one of our better pieces of business.

"If you come as a free agent it doesn't mean it costs no money because there's a salary. But we believed in him when perhaps not many were doing this.

"He also believes in himself and he believes in Leeds United, so I would say he was a perfect fit."

Farke has been dealt an injury blow as his side bid to extend their unbeaten Premier League start to five matches at home against Crystal Palace on Sunday, with summer signing Harry Wilson ruled out with a thigh injury.

"Sadly, Harry Wilson is out for this game with a quad injury. He had some problems after the [Newcastle] game. He'll also probably miss Wales' [Nations League] games."

Confidence is sky high at Elland Road after Monday's win lifted them to the dizzy heights of third place in the table.

Leeds have lost just five of their last 29 league games stretching back to last November, with only four other clubs collecting more points during that period.

Farke added: "It's no coincidence. If you deliver over a long-term period it's not just a good period, it's quality.

"Everyone can be proud, but nothing is taken for granted. Momentum can change quickly. We're fully aware if we think we are 'big time,' it's the first step to failure.

"The table is not important. Eight points after four games is good, but not what we want to achieve. Want to win 40 points as quickly as possible and our only aim is to make sure we win that."

articles.headline: Rio Ngumoha 'deserves' England call - Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola
articles.description: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has praised the attitude of forward Rio Ngumoha and said he "absolutely deserves" his call up to the England national team.
articles.body:
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has praised the attitude of forward Rio Ngumoha and said he "absolutely deserves" his call up to the England national team.

Ngumoha earned his first senior cap for England in a friendly against New Zealand back in June, having been included in Thomas Tuchel's pre-World Cup training camp.

The 18-year-old is one of a number of players who will be hoping to make an impression on the England boss in the upcoming international break, as well as midfielder Alex Scott who worked under Iraola at AFC Bournemouth.

"Very happy for both," Iraola said. "I think they both absolutely deserve it. They both also went to help the national team before the tournament and I am sure they both did a good job. I can only speak so well about both. It's very deserved, they are very ready and I hope they both enjoy it."

Ngumoha has already made five appearances for Liverpool this season and started in Tuesday's 3-1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur in the Carabao Cup. While the forward has traditionally played on the left, Iraola prefers his wingers to play on both flanks and has praised the way Ngumoha has embraced the challenge.

"The other day, for example, against Spurs he probably didn't have his best start to the game but I like how he came back from that," the Liverpool boss said. "He lost a couple of duels at the beginning. [Destiny] Udogie is a very strong player. But after, he did his job. In the first two goals, he appears. Everything comes from the situations he goes one v one and he takes good decisions.

"The play finishes on the other side but he is part of that build up for the goal and that is what we are trying to put into him. He has to still adapt to the rhythm of the league because he is still very young, he has just turned 18. But has the quality to be involved in those kind of plays and I'm liking especially his attitude, because he's not like: 'I prefer to play here.' He's ready to do what we need. I'm very happy also because they've called him for the national team."

- England Nations League squad: Trent Alexander-Arnold, Cole Palmer recalled after World Cup snub

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F

- Trent Alexander-Arnold, Cole Palmer challenged to 'perform' for England by Thomas Tuchel

This weekend will see Iraola return to the Vitality Stadium to face former club Bournemouth, where he will be hoping to oversee his second Premier League victory of the season.

Asked how he feels about facing his old team, Iraola said: "I think in the personal side I'm really looking forward to meeting and hugging them, players that I love, staff that I have worked with that I appreciate so much. I was pushing for them yesterday when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best.

"But there is another part that is the most important one right now. That we need to go there and win and beat them and be as ruthless as possible. And leave all the talking for after the game."

articles.headline: Fantasy Baseball Forecaster Playoff Round 2, Week 2: Sept. 21-27
articles.description: Set your lineups for fantasy baseball's final week with our preview featuring pitcher rankings, hitter ratings and schedule observations.
articles.body:
This is it! The final week of the 2026 fantasy baseball season has arrived. If you've made it this far, congratulations! The final seven days should be a wild race to the finish line, both in the real game and in our own leagues.

Week 25 is one of the more balanced weeks on the schedule, with one exception: The Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees begin their week-opening series with a Tuesday doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. One of those games makes up their May 23 postponement. The extra game gives both teams a seven-game final week.

All of the other 28 teams play exactly six games -- and 14 of those 28 split those six games evenly between home and the road. This is a "quality over quantity" week when it comes to matchups analysis. Additionally, most teams begin their weeks on Tuesday, as there are only three games scheduled for Monday.

Remember that MLB schedules all games on its final day, Sunday, Sept. 27, to start within a 15 minute window of one another (between 3:05 p.m. and 3:20 p.m. ET). This is by design to try and heighten the drama of real-life playoff races, but it also creates many mad, 3-4 hour dashes to the finish line in fantasy baseball leagues.

Get your popcorn -- I mean, your peanuts and Cracker Jack -- ready!

articles.body:
Latest fantasy baseball reliever updates

Pete Fairbanks returned to the injured list only days after his activation. The Marlins seem likely to use a closer-by-committee for the remainder of 2026, with Calvin Faucher and Michael Peterson the top options. (September 16)

The Nationals demoted Clayton Beeter, their top save-getter this season, to Triple-A Rochester on Sept. 12. Erik Tolman, Jack Sinclair and Will Dion seem likely to handle save chances in a committee moving forward. (September 14)

Jacob Webb blew his third consecutive save chance on Sept. 8, casting doubt on his ability to hold the Cubs' closer role. The team might choose to go the matchups route in the short term, with Daniel Palencia, Ryan Zeferjahn and Ryan Rolison candidates for ninth-inning work. (September 9)
